description:
Publish the next version of an organization skill that exists. To share a skill with the team on Valet, such as one the user keeps locally, call create_service with kind skill and then this; every member's agent can then read it. Prefer edits to change some files of a skill: each replaces or adds one file and keeps every other file, binary files included. files replaces the whole skill and drops every file it leaves out, binary files included. push publishes a commit made with create_push, which carries any file. Give one of the three, and skill with edits or push; the SKILL.md frontmatter must name the skill.

Pass base_version, the version get_skill reported, so a teammate's publish in between is not overwritten; edits need it. When the skill has moved past it, nothing is published: read the skill again and redo the change. A new skill starts with create_service with kind skill; any other name that holds no skill is refused.

Publishing under a well-known name, such as governance, security, or design-system, replaces what Valet would otherwise supply for every agent in the organization from the next read on, so do it when the user has asked to change how the organization works, and show them the content first. A well-known name is the exception to create_service: its first publish with files or edits needs no create_service, while push does. A skill named by governance is a standard; writing it requires an Admin.

Destructive because it replaces the previous version's content for every reader. Repeating a call with identical content mints no new version and reports deduped. Pass an idempotency_key so a retry after a lost answer returns the first call's result instead of publishing again. Returns the version, content hash, and commit, or evaluation without them while the release waits for its policies. Requires connecting a Valet account.

base_version.description: The version get_skill reported, 0 for Valet's default. It keeps a publish from overwriting a teammate's newer version.

edits.description: Files to change as [{path, content}], text only, paths relative to the skill root. Each replaces or adds that file; every other file is kept, binary files included, and all of them land in one new version.

content.description: The file's complete new text content.

path.description: Path of the file relative to the skill root, such as docs/guide.md.

files.description: The skill's whole tree as [{path, content}], text only, paths relative to the skill root. Must include SKILL.md, the complete definition with name and description frontmatter. Replaces the whole skill: a file it leaves out is removed, binary files included.

path.description: Path of the file relative to the skill root, such as docs/guide.md.

idempotency_key.description: An opaque key of your choosing. Repeating a call with the same key returns the first call's result instead of publishing again, which makes a retry safe.

org_name.description: The Valet organization to publish into. Omit to use the organization the account joined first.

push.description: Publish a Git push instead of files: the id create_push returned and the commit you pushed to its branch. Use it when you can run git with network access, because it sends only what changed. Every other argument keeps its meaning.

commit.description: The full sha of the commit you pushed to the push's branch. The recipe create_push returned prints it.

skill.description: The skill's name. With files, omit it to use the SKILL.md frontmatter name.

name: publish_skill

commit.description: Commit sha of the version in the skill repository. Absent while the release waits for its policies.

content_sha256.description: SHA-256 hash of the version bundle. Absent while the release waits for its policies.

deduped.description: True when the bundle matched the latest version, so no new version was minted.

evaluation.description: The release evaluation. Without version, nothing new is live: follow it with get_evaluation. With version, the release is live and this is its monitor-only evaluation. Absent when the release has none.

deploy.description: What deploy did with the release: 'waiting' for the policies, 'live', or the code of the refusal. Absent when deploy has not decided.

deploy_message.description: The refusal's message when deploy refused the release, with credentials redacted as [redacted]. Absent otherwise.

id.description: ID of the release evaluation. Pass it to get_evaluation as evaluation_id.

monitor_findings.description: Count of findings monitor policies reported on a live release. They never block it; get_evaluation shows each. Absent when zero.

monitor_running.description: Names of monitor policies still pending or running on a live release. They never block it. Absent when none are.

redactions.description: How many credentials were replaced with [redacted] in the text this answer was built from: secret values the service holds, and strings shaped like an API key, a private key, a token, or a password in a URL or header. Redaction is best effort, so 0 does not prove the text holds no credential.

status.description: Status of the evaluation across its release policies. get_evaluation lists the per-policy results.

org.description: Name of the Valet organization the call acted in.

replaced_default.description: True when the name is one Valet supplies a built-in skill for and the organization skill now answers in its place.

source.description: Where the skill content now comes from: always org, the organization skill this publish wrote.

version.description: Version number the skill now holds. Pass it to later publishes as base_version. Absent while the release waits for its policies (see evaluation).

title: Publish an organization skill
